scenario: A user-owned API key or a Codex access token leaks through a laptop, log, CI output, or pasted configuration and is used to run models or Codex as the firm.
threat_source: External attacker using a stolen credential
affected_assets: API projects; Codex workspace identity; billing
treatment: Allow only service-account keys, cap key and token lifetimes, move workloads to workload identity federation, add an IP allowlist, and enforce a hard spend limit.

scenario: A member publishes a Site or shares a GPT beyond the workspace, exposing deal or client material to anyone with the link.
affected_assets: Client documents; deal material; Sites data
treatment: Keep public Site publishing and external invitations off, limit GPT sharing to named groups, and turn off automatic Library references.

scenario: An unreviewed plugin, app, or MCP server reads mail, files, or CRM records through a broad or shared connection and sends content elsewhere.
treatment: Approve plugins per role, keep Action control read-only, scope shared connections, pin marketplace imports, and enforce the local MCP allowlist.

scenario: Web content or a document carries prompt injection that drives a cloud browser, Browser Use, Computer Use, or Codex cloud task into sending data or taking an action.
affected_assets: Connected systems; signed-in browser sessions; source code
treatment: Disable Always allow, keep code and shell internet off, block live search, disable Computer Use and external Browser Use, and keep cloud agent internet off or limited to GET.

scenario: A former employee or contractor keeps workspace access or a working Codex token after leaving because removal happened only in the workspace or the token was suspended rather than revoked.
threat_source: Former insider or takeover of a dormant account
affected_assets: Workspace chats and files; Codex automations; connected systems
treatment: Remove access at the identity provider, keep Automatic Account Creation off with SCIM, revoke leaver tokens, and move automation to service accounts.

scenario: Client data is retained longer, stored elsewhere, or processed under different terms than a client agreement allows, for example through API-key sign-in or an unset retention policy.
treatment: Record retention and residency decisions per workspace and project, restrict Codex login to ChatGPT, and use EKM where keys are required.

scenario: Runaway Work tasks, automations, or API traffic consume credits and overage far beyond budget before anyone notices.
treatment: Set per-user credit limits, a workspace overage limit other than No limit, and an API hard spend limit; alerts alone do not cap spend.

scenario: Managed policy, developer instructions, or a repository AGENTS.md file is changed without review, or a user overrides it locally, so agents run with weaker rules than approved.
threat_source: Insider error or a malicious contributor
treatment: Keep policy and instruction files in version control with review, deliver security settings as requirements, and name an owner for each policy.

scenario: A Codex session runs with approvals bypassed or full access, so a mistaken or injected command changes files, history, or remote systems without a person seeing it.
affected_assets: Source code; developer devices; remote systems
treatment: Block never and danger-full-access in requirements, enforce restrictive command rules, and export telemetry without prompt text.

scenario: An investigation needs workspace or API records older than the 30-day compliance window, or audit logging was never enabled.
treatment: Export compliance records continuously, enable API audit logging, and send Codex telemetry to a firm collector with retention.

scenario: An over-privileged workspace owner or API organization owner account is taken over and used to widen sharing, create tokens, or disable controls.
threat_source: External attacker using a phished administrator account
treatment: Enforce SSO and MFA at the identity provider, keep owner lists short, grant access through groups, and inventory Admin API keys.

scenario: Computer History, Appshots, or remote control captures or exposes sensitive on-screen or cross-app activity from a firm device.
affected_assets: Communications; financial records on the device
treatment: Keep Computer History ungranted and disable Appshots, device remote control, and Locked Use through requirements.
